Objective
Learn scale factors in similar triangles.
Dilation
A dilation changes size while keeping shape.
Corresponding
Match corresponding sides in the original and image.
Definition
Scale factor is image length divided by original length.
Enlargement
A factor greater than one means enlargement.
Reduction
A factor between zero and one means reduction.
Length rule
Multiply original length by the scale factor.
Length example
Three becomes nine, so the factor is three.
Inverse
Divide image length by k to recover original length.
Perimeter
Perimeter scales by k, just like every side.
Perimeter example
Perimeter eighteen with factor three becomes fifty four.
Area
Area scales by the square of k.
Area example
Area eighty with factor one half becomes twenty.
Why square
Width and height both scale, so multiply k by k.
Area to scale
Take the positive square root of image area over original area.
Area ratio
Sixteen becomes one hundred forty four; k is three.
Similarity
All corresponding side ratios must match.
Units
Lengths have units, areas have squared units.
Mistake
Do not multiply area by k instead of k squared.
Check
Always divide image by original in the same order.
Next step
Practice eighteen questions and complete the five-question test.
